problem: The text states 'Numerical aperture is NA = sin θa', but that is only true when the outside medium is air (n0 = 1). The general definition carries n0, and later parts of the chapter (Q7, exam traps) use the general form, so the definition line is inconsistent.
fix: Numerical aperture is defined by NA = n0 sin θa = √(n1² − n2²); with air outside (n0 = 1) it reduces to NA = sin θa.

problem: 'A wider cone ... usually means a larger core and more modes' is loose. A larger NA by itself raises the mode count (V depends on NA and core radius); it does not imply a larger core.
fix: A wider cone, meaning larger n1² − n2², accepts more rays. That helps coupling, but a larger NA also supports more modes, which can spread the pulse; see Unit 2, Intermodal dispersion.
